summary: Intermittent 429s for mobile upload pipeline — path normalization & shared-proxy multiplexing causing double quota consumption
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 responses from the hosted API when their mobile app uploads attachments. The errors started after a CDN rollout and proxy config change. Impact: ~4% of upload requests from the eu-west mobile cohort are rejected with 429 for the last 48 hours, causing failed user uploads and retry storms from the mobile SDK. Observed behavior: 429s are clustered around a small subset of clients behind the same corporate proxy/NAT. Many of the failing requests show identical path variants (trailing slash vs no trailing slash) and alternate authorization token headers due to ephemeral key refreshes. Expected behavior: Uploads should be accepted (or gracefully backoff) and counted once against the tenant quota. Throttles should reflect actual token usage, not duplicate counting produced by proxy multiplexing or edge normalization.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the mobile SDK with ephemeral API key rotation enabled (rotate every ~30s).
2) Send concurrent multipart upload requests over a single HTTP/2 connection through a shared corporate proxy that normalizes paths (adds/removes trailing slash) and rewrites cookies/SNI headers.
3) Observe 429 responses intermittently after the CDN/edge proxy rollout (approx 4% of requests).
4) Capture X-Request-ID and X-Quota-Trace headers from success and failure attempts for comparison.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:40:12Z samples show same conn id and two distinct path forms counted within same refill window causing effective +1 charge for identical user action.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (support): Customer reports spike after CDN config pushed 2026-03-08. Provided X-Request-ID slices and sample SDK versions (android-sdk 2.3.1, ios-sdk 2.3.0). Asked for quota traces.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Investigating edge-proxy logs. Early hypothesis: connection multiplexing + path normalization causing two logical request records for a single user action. Pulling edge counter logs and billing write traces.
2026-03-11 - Peregrine Analytics (Customer): Confirmed failures concentrated in corporate NATs and via their partner CDN. They can reproduce locally using a proxy that strips trailing slashes.

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Scoped a test that sends identical requests with/without trailing slash; edge shows two counter entries when requests traverse HTTP/2 connection reuse with path normalization enabled.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy path normalization (trailing slash rewrite) causes canonicalization mismatch between ingress counting layer and billing actor, creating duplicate count events when the same HTTP/2 stream is reused.

Hypothesis 2: Ephemeral key rotate event mid-request leads to two auth headers being present across connection reuse; quota layer attributes charge to both token hashes leading to tenant double billing in same window.

Data pulled: edge counter logs (2026-03-09 22:14 - 22:20), billing write audit (consumer=tenant-125), connection multiplexer traces. Pattern: same conn_id + two path variants within 500ms window; second record increments tenant quota again.

Attempted repro in staging w/ our proxy: reproduced duplicate counter when request transform (add/remove trailing slash) is applied post-multiplex demux. Repro steps saved to test-run: edge-proxy/test/ratecount-multiplex-20260311.
Risk: high — double counting inflates quota consumption and triggers 429s for customer; affects enterprise tenants behind certain proxies and CDN rules.
resolution: Workaround (short term): Recommended customer disable path-normalization rule on their partner CDN / corporate proxy for Redwood API paths, or configure SDK to persist canonical path (always include trailing slash). Also suggested increasing tenant burst pool temporarily (support action) to avoid user impact while fix is implemented.

Mitigation (engineering): Edge team to add normalization step earlier in the request pipeline before quota accounting or to dedupe accounting events by canonical request fingerprint (conn_id + canonical_path + tenant_id + event_timestamp window).

Rollout plan: 1) Patch edge-proxy to canonicalize path before counting (canary in eu-west small shard) 2) Monitor quota-write deltas and 429 rates for the affected tenant cohort 3) Full rollout after 48h of stable metrics. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1422
Follow-ups: Postmortem with CDN partner to clarify rules that triggered normalization; update troubleshooting doc with guidance for customers using corporate proxies or CDNs that rewrite paths.
